SOLANUM   ARREBENTA.     (VELL.)

SOL.  AR.       PORTUG.:       ARREBEN'TA    CAVALLOS.


THIS  bush  grows  spontaneously  in  the  provinces  of  Rio
Janeiro,  along  roads  and  in  cultivated  places.  It  is  from  10
to  16  inches  high  ;  its  branches  which  bifurcate  regularly,
are,  while  young,  covered  with  strong  thorns  growing  from
above  downwards.  Leaves  slightly  pubescent,  cordate,  with
five  obtuse  lobes  ;  their  nerves  are  furnished  with  a  few  irre-
gularly distributed  thorns.  The  flowers  are  supported  by
peduncles  arising  from  the  axils  of  the  leaves  in  groups  of
two  or  three.  Calix  with  five  parts,  very  prickly  on  the
outside  ;  corol  with  five  divisions  ;  five  stamens  ;  a  style.
Berry  red,  fleshy,  with  two  chambers,  containing  a  large
number  of  small  seeds.  Roots  fibrous,  arising  from  a  com-
mon rhizoma.  We  use  the  leaves.
